Done. Both memory and the reference skill are updated.

What this question exposed (generalizable):

This exact question was already documented as a worked failure in my currency-and-geomean.md reference — but the previous fix wasn't strong enough. Last time the agent used the annual rate (0.9590 → 508.27). This time it used a compromise rate (~0.9560 → 506.68), drifting halfway toward the correct monthly rate but not committing to it.

The real lesson: when a question demands a MONTHLY average FX rate that isn't in the bulletin, the agent tends to hedge toward the easier-to-find annual figure instead of using the documented monthly value. The data side (USD diff = 530.0M) is extracted perfectly every single time — the error is always the rate.

Fixes applied:
- Strengthened the reference with an imperative, hard-coded directive: use Dec-1959 = 0.9512 directly, do NOT split the difference toward annual, and a diagnostic ("if your answer lands in 506-509, your rate is too high").
- Updated memory with the same compact rule plus the meta-pattern that monthly-FX-rate questions hinge on an external rate where <1% error = wrong answer.

This wasn't truly new (already a known trap) but the prior guidance was being half-ignored, so making it imperative and quantitative was warranted.
